newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Ross brings Arafat, Israelis together.
newsitem.headline: Ross brings Arafat, Israelis together.

text.p: U.S. envoy Dennis Ross has brought about the first meeting between Israeli officials and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat since an Islamic militant bombing deepened the crisis in Middle East peace efforts last month.
But Israel has reiterated that it will only be satisfied if it sees concrete results to its demand that Arafat crack down on militants.
On another front, Israel confirmed on Sunday that pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas had killed an Israeli soldier in deepening violence in its south Lebanon occupation zone.

Arafat met Israeli government officials on Sunday for the first time since 15 people, including the attackers, died in the July 30 bombing of an Israeli market, a Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) official said.

The official told Reuters Ross brought Israeli negotiator Yitzhak Molho and Shin Bet secret police chief Ami Ayalon with him to a meeting with Arafat in the West Bank Palestinian enclave of Ramallah. He said a third Israeli was with the group but he did not have his name.
At the end of the Ramallah meeting, the second between Ross and Arafat on Sunday, another PLO official, who also spoke on condition he not be named, said:

"The parties have agreed to resume trilateral security meetings. Another trilateral meeting will be held tomorrow. They discussed the basis on which these meetings would be carried out. These meetings would pave the way for the political meetings," he said.
Israeli officials were not immediately available to comment.
Ross's delegation travelled to Ramallah from Jerusalem where Ross had just ended his second meeting of the day with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Netanyahu, in a speech before his second meeting with Ross which was broadcast in part later by Israel Radio, said: "Certainly, meetings are possible of security officials, between us and the Palestinian Authority, possibly also with American participation, soon.
"And things will be evaluated not by statements, not by pretty words, things will be evaluated on the extent to which the Palestinian Authority fulfils their commitments..."
Netanyahu has said peace talks will not resume until Arafat cracks down on militants as he says Arafat pledged to do in peace deals. Arafat says he has fought them.

Negotiations between the sides, already in crisis over Israel beginning a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March, hit a new low after the market bombing. Netanyahu suspended peace talks and sealed off the West Bank and Gaza.
"I have a sense that there's a desire to find ways to move forward but it will take a lot of work," Ross told Israel's Channel Two television.
Arafat wants Israel to stop the Arab East Jerusalem settlement, end Palestinian house demolitions and land confiscations, and lift the closure of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Israel vows to continue the East Jerusalem settlement.

Ross said U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright was prepared to visit the region at the end of the month provided progress was made on security. Her trip would probably be aimed at finding ways to wrap up outstanding issues from interim Israel-PLO deals and pursue accelerated final negotiations.

The Israeli army lifted an "inner closure" in parts of the West Bank on Sunday, allowing Palestinians to travel between three besieged self-ruled cities -- Jenin, Tulkarm and Qalqilya. A siege of Jericho and Nablus was lifted on Friday.
It opened crossings linking the West Bank and Gaza with Jordan and Egypt for travel by Palestinians and others. Palestinians are still barred from Israel.

The Israeli soldier's death brought the toll to 15 in the bloodiest week in south Lebanon since an Israeli offensive in April, 1996 Apart from the soldier, a pro-Israeli militiaman, six members of Hizbollah and seven Lebanese civilians have died.
